title: The Fox and the North Wind
logline: When the north wind blows for three nights, a white fox comes to the door and must be given a gift. This time, Nell has to answer.
style: 3D diorama toon: chunky stylized 3D models with flat cel shading (2-3 tone bands) and black ink outlines, warm cream/sepia palette, red-painted Swedish wood, deep Arctic-blue night.

narrator.notes: Warm, unhurried storyteller reading a bedtime story to a 10-year-old. Gentle pauses at commas. Never theatrical.

farmor.notes: An old Swedish grandmother speaking English carefully, with small pauses, the way people do when translating in their head. Quiet, warm, a little solemn.

nell.notes: A curious, brave 10-year-old girl. Natural and soft, a little breathless when nervous.

nell.description: Nell, a 10-year-old girl with long straight brown hair, rosy cheeks and brown eyes, wearing a dark grey wool coat, a knitted hat and snow boots
nell.refPrompt: Character model sheet of Nell, a 10-year-old girl with long straight brown hair, rosy cheeks and brown eyes, wearing a dark grey wool coat, a knitted hat and snow boots. Three views side by side: front, three-quarter, side. Full body, neutral pose, plain cream paper background.

Three views side by side: front, three-quarter, side. Full body, neutral pose, plain cream paper background.

shots.description: Exterior, night: the camera glides low over the frozen lake toward the small red house; aurora, falling snow. Nell walks through the snow pulling a suitcase to the lit door.

lines.text: This is where Nell spent Christmas when she was ten, in her grandmother's small red house at the edge of a frozen lake.

shots.description: Inside by the wood stove: Farmor sits and tells the family story; Nell sits wrapped in a blanket, listening. Firelight.

lines.text: When the north wind blows for three nights, the fox comes to the door. And a gift must be given. Honestly.

shots.description: Closer two-shot of Nell and Farmor by the fire.

lines.text: Then the fox takes something else.

shots.description: Night: the north wind drives snow around the corners of the house; the camera drifts down to small fresh fox tracks leading to the front door.

lines.text: That night, the wind came out of the north, humming one long, low note around the corners of the house.

shots.description: Flashback in blue: a gold necklace lies on the doorstep. The white fox walks up, looks at it, turns and walks away.

lines.text: Once, I gave a gold necklace. The fox looked at it, and left. The next morning, my father's silver ring was gone.

shots.description: The third night, by the front door inside: Nell in coat and hat holds the small wooden box; Farmor nods.

lines.text: By morning, Nell knew what she would give.
I need to do this on my own.

shots.description: The doorstep in bright moonlight: the fox walks out of the pines and sits in the snow facing Nell.

lines.text: The fox was smaller than she had expected. White as the snow. Eyes of amber.

shots.description: Nell sings, the box at her feet; the wind drops and the snow slows almost to a stop.

lines.text: Vem kan segla förutan vind, vem kan ro utan åror.
lines.subtitle:
♪ Vem kan segla förutan vind? Vem kan ro utan åror? ♪
(Who can sail without wind? Who can row without oars?)

shots.description: The fox bows its head over the box, turns and walks back into the trees.

lines.text: The fox bowed its head, once, like someone accepting a gift, and was gone.

shots.description: Inside by the fire: Farmor, moved to tears; Nell beside her.
Dawn in the still forest: the small white fox walks home between the pines, growing smaller.

lines.text: Somewhere far off, a small white fox carried something home that only it could hear.
